environment.description: Same application deployed on Tomcat 9.0.65. Database connectivity routed through PgBouncer 1.18 configured in transaction pooling mode with a custom query parser module (pgbouncer-rr with routing rules). The PostgreSQL 14 database user is configured with a SECURITY DEFINER function wrapper: all queries must be executed through a stored procedure `exec_report(text)` which internally uses `pg_parse_query()` (from pg_query extension) to parse the SQL AST and rejects any statement containing more than one DML command, any DDL, any subquery in WHERE clauses referencing `pg_catalog` or `information_schema`, or any UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT operators. The DB role used by the application (`app_report_ro`) has SELECT privilege ONLY on views `v_sales_report`, `v_inventory_report`, `v_users_report` — no direct table access. Additionally, PostgreSQL `log_statement = 'all'` with a pg_audit trigger that terminates connections issuing queries not matching a whitelist regex pattern `^SELECT\s+(product_name|item_name|username|email|last_login|quantity|amount|sale_date|last_updated|created_at|SUM\(amount\))`. The DB role has `statement_timeout = 2000` preventing time-based blind injection, and `row_limit` (via pg_plan_filter extension) caps result sets at 1000 rows.

config.proxy: PgBouncer 1.18 transaction mode with pgbouncer-rr routing
config.db_role: app_report_ro with SELECT on views only, no direct table grants
config.stored_procedure_gate: exec_report(text) with pg_parse_query AST validation: rejects UNION, multi-statement, DDL, information_schema/pg_catalog subqueries
config.audit: pg_audit with connection termination on non-whitelisted patterns
